title: Remove legacy XML token parser and stage JOSE-based JWT runtime with KMS-backed signing
creator: Samir Patel
description: Context: The legacy SAML/XML and token parsing stack (xmlsec wrapper + custom JWT parsing shim) continues to be a high-risk maintenance area. We observe intermittent parsing failures, inconsistent canonicalization behavior, and several transitive vulnerabilities surfaced by the recent SBOM review. Goal: Replace the bespoke XML token parsing path and the in-house JWT parser with a JOSE-compliant runtime-backed implementation, integrate KMS-based signing (customer key migration plan), and build an OpenSSL compatibility shim that supports both FIPS-compatible builds and our current non-FIPS hosted fleet. Scope: - Replace xmlsec-dependent SAML validation path with a hardened native verifier module (drop external xmlsec binary dependencies). - Migrate token ingestion to go-jose / python-jose (service-specific choices) and canonicalize token acceptance policy. - Introduce a small compatibility shim at the runtime layer to handle legacy tokens for a 30-day coexistence window. - Build CI gating and fuzzing tests for token parsers and SAML canonicalization. - Coordinate KMS signing rollout (customers on dedicated/private will be prompted, hosted keys migrated via strategy). Considerations: - Maintain zero-downtime for hosted API by routing old parser to shaded canary pool for 2 weeks while new parser handles main traffic. - Ensure OpenSSL 3.1 build path (with FIPS provider) is tested across GPU inference hosts and administrative tooling. - Preserve audit logs and add token-verification telemetry for early regressions.
acceptance_criteria: New JOSE-based parser (service-auth) passes full unit + integration suite and performance regression <5% CPU at peak
SAML verifier removes external xmlsec binary dependency and produces bit-for-bit consistent assertions for canonical test suite
Compatibility shim correctly routes legacy tokens and is removable after 30 days with no customer errors >0.1%
KMS signing integration documented and key migration runbook published
Security review completed and high/critical vulnerabilities remediated in transitive deps
